class.name: MySQLResult
class.brief_description: The outcome of an [code]execute_*[/code] call: rows, metadata and error, never an exception.
class.description: Returned by every synchronous [code]execute_*[/code] method of [MySQLSession] (and, inside a [MySQLAsyncOperation], by the asynchronous ones). Always check [method is_ok] before reading rows: on failure, [method get_rows] and the other accessors return empty values instead of anything meaningful, and the reason is in [method get_error]. Holds every resultset of the call, in order (usually one; more than one when [member MySQLConfig.allow_multi_queries] is on, or when running a stored procedure that returns several). Most accessors take a [code]resultset[/code] index, defaulting to [code]0[/code]. Rows are returned as an [Array] of [Array]s, one inner [Array] per row with the values in column order, never as a [Dictionary] keyed by column name: a [code]JOIN[/code] can produce duplicate column names, which a [Dictionary] could not keep separate.

method.name: get_affected_rows
method.description: Number of rows affected by an [code]INSERT[/code]/[code]UPDATE[/code]/[code]DELETE[/code] in the given resultset. An [int], or a [String] holding the exact value for the rare case of a count above what a 64-bit signed integer can hold.

method.name: get_column_names
method.description: Column names of the given resultset, in order. May contain duplicates (see the class description).

method.name: get_error
method.description: The error, if [method is_ok] is [code]false[/code]; an empty [Dictionary] otherwise. Has the keys [code]category[/code] ([String], for example [code]"mysql.common-server"[/code] for a server-reported error or [code]"mysql_module.client"[/code] for one detected by the module itself before talking to the server), [code]message[/code] ([String]), [code]server_message[/code] ([String], empty for a client-side error) and [code]is_fatal[/code] ([bool], [code]true[/code] if the connection itself is no longer usable, for example after a failed TLS handshake).

method.name: get_info
method.description: The server's informational message for the given resultset, if any (for example, the row counts an [code]INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE[/code] reports). Usually empty for a plain [code]SELECT[/code].

method.name: get_last_insert_id
method.description: The [code]AUTO_INCREMENT[/code] value generated by an [code]INSERT[/code] in the given resultset, or [code]0[/code] if none was generated. An [int], or a [String] for the rare case of a value above what a 64-bit signed integer can hold.

method.name: get_parsed_json
method.description: Parses one cell as JSON and returns the result (cached, so calling this again for the same cell is free). Only makes sense when [member MySQLConfig.json_result_mode] is [constant MySQLConfig.LAZY_PARSED_VARIANT] (the default), where [method get_rows] keeps the raw text instead of parsing eagerly; in the other modes the cell already comes ready from [method get_rows]. Does not check that the column is a [code]JSON[/code] one: naming a cell here is already saying "this is JSON". If the text is not valid JSON, returns [code]null[/code] (same as [method JSON.parse_string]).

method.name: get_resultset_count
method.description: Number of resultsets held by this result. Usually [code]1[/code]; see the class description for when there can be more.

method.name: get_rows
method.description: Rows of the given resultset. See the class description for the shape (an [Array] of [Array]s).

method.name: is_ok
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the call succeeded. When [code]false[/code], read [method get_error] for why; every other accessor returns an empty/default value instead of real data.
